headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here are a few well‑known public APIs that accept an IP address and return business‑related data (company name, industry, size, contact details, etc.). All of them offer a free tier (with limits) and paid plans for higher volume or richer data. | Service | Key Features | Free Tier | Paid Plans | Example Endpoint | |---------|--------------|-----------|------------|------------------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Company name, domain, industry, employee count
• Contact email & phone (if available)
• Geo‑location, ASN, carrier | 50 k requests/month, 1 k per day | $5–$25/month (up to 1 M req/month) | `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=YOUR_TOKEN` | | **ipstack.com** | • Organization name, domain, industry
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, currency, timezone | 10 k requests/month | $10–$200/month (up to 5 M req/month) | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=YOUR_KEY&format=1` | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization name, domain, industry
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, ASN, carrier | 30 k requests/month | $9–$99/month (up to 1 M req/month) | `https://ipapi.co//json/?key=YOUR_KEY` | | **ipdata.co** | • Company name, domain, industry, size
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, ASN, carrier | 50 k requests/month | $10–$200/month (up to 1 M req/month) | `https://api.ipdata.co/?api-key=YOUR_KEY` | | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Organization name, domain, industry
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, ASN, carrier | 30 k requests/month | $10–$200/month (up to 1 M req/month) | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=` | ### How to use one of them (example with ipinfo.io) ```bash # Replace with the target IP address and YOUR_TOKEN with your API token curl "https://ipinfo.io//json?token=YOUR_TOKEN" ``` Sample JSON response: ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If you enable the paid plan, the response will include fields such as: ```json { "company": { "name": "Google LLC", "domain": "google.com", "industry": "Internet Services", "size": "100000+", "contact": { "email": "support@google.com", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000" } } } ``` ### Things to keep in mind 1. **Privacy & Legal** – Some jurisdictions restrict the collection of personal data. Make sure you comply with GDPR, CCPA, etc., especially if you store or process contact emails/phones. 2. **Rate Limits** – Free tiers usually cap daily requests. If you need bulk lookups, consider a paid plan or batch processing. 3. **Data Accuracy** – Contact details are often optional and may be missing or outdated. Verify critical data before using it in production. 4. **Caching** – IP addresses don’t change often. Cache responses locally (e.g., Redis, in‑memory cache) to reduce API calls and stay within rate limits. Feel free to pick the provider that best matches your budget and feature needs. If you need help integrating a specific API into your stack (Node.js, Python, etc.), let me know!
